# `silk/system/filesystem_native`

<!-- Generated by silk doc-reference. Do not edit by hand. -->

The native provider of the `FileSystem` effect, confined to one directory of the host.

## When to use
Provide [`OsFileSystem`](#OsFileSystem) for `FileSystem` in a native program. Code that uses files uses
`silk.system.filesystem`, so a test can provide a file system in memory.

## Details
[`OsFileSystem.make`](#OsFileSystem.impl.make) takes a root directory of the host. The path `/` of the provider is that
root, not the root of the host. A path cannot leave the root: `..` is not valid in a `Path`, and
the Unix provider resolves a symbolic link below the root inside the root. An absolute link
target starts again at the root, and `..` in a target never goes above it. Windows also confines
relative link targets, holding each traversed directory open. Absolute Windows symlink and
junction targets must name the native root or a descendant, with matching component spelling
except drive-letter case. Other absolute targets return `Unsupported`. Both providers limit
resolution to 40 links; a cycle fails with `InvalidPath`.

The write operations are different:
- `writeFile` creates or truncates the file, then writes. If it fails, a partial file can stay.
- `createFile` fails with `AlreadyExists` if the entry exists. If a later write fails, the new
  partial file stays.
- `writeFileAtomic` writes a temporary file in the same directory, then renames it to the path
  (to replace) or links it (to create). A reader sees the old file or the complete new file,
  never a part. A replace changes a final symbolic link itself, not its target.

On Unix, new files get mode 0666, filtered by the umask of the process. An atomic replace makes a new
file, so the permissions, owner, extended attributes, and hard links of the old file are not
kept. A synchronized atomic write calls `fsync` on the file before the rename, and on the
directory after it. `syncDirectory` also uses `fsync`. These do not use `F_FULLFSYNC`, and do
not promise that data survives a power loss.

On WASI, roots name preopened guest directories. The host controls rights, file permissions, and synchronization support.

On Windows, roots are normalized absolute drive or UNC paths, such as `C:\work` or `\\server\share`, separate from portable `Path` values.
Root bytes and path bytes must be canonical WTF-8. Device roots are unsupported.
The provider requires NTFS, preserves case, and inherits permissions for new files.
UNC supports ordinary reads, writes, creation, inspection, and listing. Remote atomic publication is
refused before staging; deletion requires server support for POSIX disposition and otherwise fails.
Buffered publication uses one handle rename; create-only publication never replaces an existing entry.
Known final links can be listed, removed, or replaced. Unknown reparse tags are unsupported.
Directory synchronization and synchronized publication fail with `Unsupported` before publication.
Windows provider codes are signed NTSTATUS bit patterns, not `GetLastError` values.

Directory listings are sorted by the bytes of the paths. A native error becomes a `FileError`
with a portable reason and the native code.

## Errors
- `FileError` for each failed operation. If a close fails after an earlier error, the earlier
  error is returned.
- `AtomicWriteError` from `writeFileAtomic`. It tells if the failure was before or after the new
  contents became visible, and names a temporary file that cleanup could not remove.
- `OutOfMemoryError` from operations that return owned bytes or paths.

## Gotchas
- Trust the root and its parent directories. The confinement does not protect against a process
  that renames those directories, changes mounts, or changes the temporary files.
- After `writeFileAtomic` fails with a published error, the new contents are visible. Do not
  write again without a check.
- The provider exists on WASI, Darwin aarch64, GNU/Linux x86_64 or aarch64, and Windows x86_64 with system DLLs.

## Examples
### Write and read a file in a temporary directory
```silk
import silk.mem.allocator { Allocator, OutOfMemoryError }
import silk.collections.bytes { Bytes }
import silk.core.effect { Effect }
import silk.system.filesystem { FileError, FileSystem, Path }
import silk.system.filesystem_native { OsFileSystem }

effect fn program() -> i32
  ! FileError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut FileSystem | &mut Allocator {
  // `/` is the root of the provider: /tmp on the host.
  let root = run Path.make("/")
  let scratch = run FileSystem.temporaryDirectory(&root, "silk-doc-")
  let file = run Path.join(&scratch.path, "note.txt")
  run FileSystem.writeFile(&file, b"hello")
  let bytes = run FileSystem.readFile(&file)
  let read = Bytes.asSlice(&bytes)
  let same = read.length == 5 && read[0] == 104
  drop read

  // Remove the directory and the file in it.
  run FileSystem.release(move scratch)
  if !same {
    return 1
  }
  return 0
}

effect fn failed<E>(error: E) -> i32 {
  drop error
  return 1
}

effect fn withFiles() -> i32
  ! FileError | OutOfMemoryError
  ? &mut Allocator {
  let mut files = run OsFileSystem.make("/tmp")
  return run program() |> Effect.provideMut<FileSystem>(&mut files)
}

pub fn main() -> i32 {
  let mut allocator = Allocator.systemAllocatorProvider()
  return run Effect.catchAll(withFiles(), failed) |> Effect.provideMut<Allocator>(&mut allocator)
}
```

Import as `OsFileSystem` with `import silk.system.filesystem_native { OsFileSystem }`.

## `OsFileSystem`

```silk
pub struct OsFileSystem
```

The native `FileSystem` provider. It owns the bytes of its root directory.

### Details
Each `Path` is resolved below the root. The root is never shown as a `Path`. An operation that
would leave the root fails. The path `/` of the provider is the root, not the root of the
host. The Unix provider resolves symbolic links below the root inside the root. On Unix, new files
get mode 0666, filtered by the umask of the process. Directory listings are sorted by the
bytes of the paths. A native error becomes a `FileError` with a portable reason and the native code.

On WASI, the root names a preopened guest directory. The host controls rights, permissions, and synchronization support.

On Windows, the root is a normalized absolute drive path, such as `C:\work`. Path bytes must be canonical WTF-8.
Local NTFS is required. New files inherit permissions. Case and lone UTF-16 surrogates are preserved.
Relative Windows link targets stay inside the root; parent components stop there. Absolute
symlink and junction targets must name the same native root or a descendant, with matching
component spelling except drive-letter case. Other absolute targets, unknown reparse tags,
and directory synchronization fail with `Unsupported`. Resolution is limited to 40 links.
Buffered publication uses one handle rename. Synchronized publication fails before any file is created.
Read-only deletion is refused. Native error codes are signed NTSTATUS bit patterns, not Win32 error codes.

### Gotchas
- Trust the root and its parent directories. The confinement does not protect against a
  process that renames those directories, changes mounts, or changes the temporary files of
  `writeFileAtomic`.
- `writeFile` and `createFile` can leave a partial file when a write fails. Use
  `writeFileAtomic` when a reader must see the old file or the complete new file.
- Synchronized writes use `fsync`, not `F_FULLFSYNC`, and do not promise that data survives a
  power loss.
- The provider exists on WASI, Darwin aarch64, GNU/Linux x86_64 or aarch64, and Windows x86_64 with system DLLs.

<a id="OsFileSystem.impl.make"></a>

### Associated function `make`

```silk
pub effect fn make(root: string) -> OsFileSystem ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a provider with a copy of the text `root` as its root directory. It does not open the directory.
Unix roots include `"/tmp"`. Windows roots use normalized absolute drive or UNC paths, such as `"C:\\work"` or `"\\\\server\\share"`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the copy cannot be allocated.

#### Gotchas
`root` must be an absolute host path, not empty, with no NUL. Other values trap.
Windows rejects device, verbatim, slash-rooted, and drive-relative paths, plus empty, `.` or `..` components.
UNC requires both a server and a share. Remote publication is unsupported; deletion needs POSIX server support.
A Windows root uses backslashes and has no trailing separator, except at the drive root.

<a id="OsFileSystem.impl.makeBytes"></a>

### Associated function `makeBytes`

```silk
pub effect fn makeBytes(root: &[u8]) -> OsFileSystem ! OutOfMemoryError ? &mut Allocator
```

Returns a provider with a copy of `root` as its root directory. It does not open the
directory. On Windows, the bytes must be canonical WTF-8; lone UTF-16 surrogates are preserved.
On Unix, the bytes do not have to be valid UTF-8.

#### When to use
Use it for a root that you got from the host as bytes, such as the working directory from
`HostInput.workingDirectory`.

#### Errors
`OutOfMemoryError` if the copy cannot be allocated.

#### Gotchas
`root` must be an absolute host path, not empty, with no NUL. Other values trap.
Windows requires a normalized absolute drive or UNC path with backslashes, such as `C:\work` or `\\server\share`.
Device, verbatim, slash-rooted, and drive-relative roots are rejected, as are noncanonical WTF-8 bytes.
UNC requires both a server and a share. Remote publication is unsupported; deletion needs POSIX server support.
Empty, `.` and `..` components and trailing separators are rejected, except the separator at the drive root.
